title: [YouPass Collect] - Qualifications of staff in an advertising company: 1990 vs 2010
prompt: The charts below show the qualifications of staff in an advertising company in 1990 and 2010. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts compare the proportions of employees with different qualifications, categorized by Science and Art fields, in an advertising company in two separate years, 1990 and 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while Ph.D.-Science experienced the most significant growth over the 20-year period, First Degree-Art witnessed the sharpest decline. Additionally, Ph.D.-Science rose to become the largest category by 2010.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with Science qualifications, in 1990, Master-Science was the most common, representing 29% of the workforce, followed by First Degree-Science at 20% and Ph.D.-Science at just 13%. By 2010, the proportion of Ph.D.-Science holders had more than doubled to 30%, making it the dominant qualification in the company and surpassing Master-Science for the first time. Meanwhile, Master-Science remained unchanged at its original figure of 29%, whereas First Degree-Science dropped considerably to just 11%, less than half of Master-Science's share.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding Art qualifications, Master-Art was the most prevalent in 1990, at 21%, while First Degree-Art and Ph.D.-Art accounted for smaller proportions of 15% and a mere 2%, respectively. Over the following two decades, First Degree-Art experienced a dramatic fall, plummeting to only 2% by 2010, making it the smallest category alongside its 1990 Ph.D.-Art counterpart. In contrast, both Ph.D.-Art and Master-Art saw slight increases, with the former more than doubling to 5% and the latter rising to 23%, respectively, by the end of the period.
